title: KPT family review
focus: Retrieve the learned KPT families and strong–weak relationship.

exercises.prompt: hattu (“hat”) → ____ (“of the hat”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: The ending -n is supplied. Recall the weak stem: tt becomes t, giving hatu-. Add -n: hatun (“of the hat”).

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT double consonants: strong grade retained
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The ending is correct, but tt must become t: hatu- + n = hatun.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT double consonants: form not yet correct

exercises.prompt: lippu (“ticket”) → ____ (“of the ticket”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: The ending -n is supplied. The double pp becomes p in the weak stem lipu-. Add -n: lipun (“of the ticket”).

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT double consonants: strong grade retained
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Keep the supplied -n, but weaken pp to p: lipu- + n = lipun.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT double consonants: form not yet correct

exercises.prompt: pöytä (“table”) → ____ (“of the table”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: The ending -n is supplied. The single t changes to d: pöydä- + n = pöydän (“of the table”).

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT common single consonants: strong grade retained
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The ending is correct. Change t to d in the weak stem: pöydän.

exercises.prompt: hakea (“to fetch”), supplied stem hake- + minä -n → ____ (“I fetch”)
exercises.explanation: The stem hake- and minä ending -n are supplied. In the weak stem, k disappears: hae- + n = haen (“I fetch”).

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT common single consonants: strong grade retained
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The single k disappears before the supplied ending: hae- + n = haen.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT common single consonants: form not yet correct

exercises.prompt: puku (“suit”) → ____ (“of the suit”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: Recall the taught pair puku–puvun. Here k changes to v, giving puvu-. Add the supplied -n: puvun (“of the suit”). This is a learned special-k pattern, not a rule for every k.

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT special k changes: special weak stem missed
answerDiagnostics.explanation: For this taught word, use puvu-. Do not keep k or simply remove it: puvu- + n = puvun.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT special k changes: weak stem not yet correct

exercises.prompt: poika (“boy”) → ____ (“of the boy”) · use the supplied genitive ending -n
exercises.explanation: Recall the taught pair poika–pojan and the weak stem poja-. In this word, k disappears and i changes to j. Add the supplied -n: pojan (“of the boy”). Learn the whole pair; simply replacing k with j would give the wrong stem.

answerDiagnostics.category: KPT special k changes: special weak stem missed
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The taught weak stem is poja-, with oj rather than oi. Add the supplied -n to get pojan.
